children: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA, Financials) may be making another multibillion-dollar gamble on one of its biggest clients. The chipmaker is the primary provider of processors used to train and operate artificial intelligence models.

The firm is reportedly considering putting up to $10 billion into Anthropic's possible initial public offering. Anthropic's IPO may value the company at roughly $2 trillion and raise as much as $100 billion. The terms are still being negotiated.
The possible investment would strengthen Nvidia's partnership with Anthropic and give the chipmaker a stake in any rise in the AI developer's valuation.
It might also return some of that capital to Nvidia in future purchases of GPUs and computing systems. The circular relationship is more complex as it pertains to the investor discussion.
Big bets by chipmakers on their own clients can make it tougher to tell how much underlying AI demand is building up on its own.
Shares of Nvidia fell almost 3% in premarket trading, as chip stocks dipped after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and other leaders in AI called for slowing the growth of frontier AI.

The question for investors isn't whether Nvidia can afford another big AI bet. The question is whether ever-larger investments across the ecosystem are producing lasting demand, or making the AI expenditure cycle harder to understand.

title: Nvidia eyes a $10 billion Anthropic bet at an awkward moment
